techStack: noUnusedLocals and noUnusedParameters enforced — every new ref must be used in JSX or logic or the build fails
eslint-plugin-react-hooks active with exhaustive-deps — dependency arrays must be correct
useLayoutEffect is safe (pure client-side SPA, no SSR), fires synchronously before paint
jsdom supports element.focus() and document.activeElement; portal via document.body means elements are in the document and natively focusable
Build command: tsc -b && vite build — TypeScript errors block the build
features: ProductDetailPanel renders via ReactDOM.createPortal into document.body — panel DOM exists in document when useLayoutEffect fires
isOpen = productId !== null; early return null sits after all hooks
panelRef (HTMLDivElement) is already attached to the panel div but currently unused — can be used for querySelectorAll in Tab-trap
Close button (detail-close-btn, aria-label='Close panel') is the first interactive element in the panel; has no ref attached yet
Backdrop div.detail-backdrop onClick={onClose} already works — must not regress
Scroll-lock useEffect (depends on [isOpen]) already in place — new effects must not conflict
Data-fetch useEffect (depends on [productId]) resets product/isLoading/error — during loading only the close button is focusable
Tests in productDetailFocus.test.tsx render full <App />, stub fetch, and test open/close/backdrop — 5 tests must pass
ProductDetailPanel is only rendered in ProductListPage.tsx; onClose = () => setDetailProductId(null)
architecture: Hook order convention: state → refs → derived constants → useEffect blocks → early return → JSX
New refs (closeButtonRef, prevFocusRef) go immediately after panelRef declaration (currently line 18)
New useLayoutEffect (focus-on-open + prev-focus capture/restore) goes after the two existing useEffect blocks, before the if (!isOpen) return null guard
New useEffect for document-level Escape listener also goes in that same zone (after scroll-lock effect)
Tab-trap logic belongs as an onKeyDown prop on the panel div — requirements 2 and 3 explicitly specify 'the panel div's onKeyDown handler'
Escape must use document.addEventListener (not onKeyDown prop) — requirement 4 is explicit; document-level listener fires even when focus is outside the panel
No component currently uses useLayoutEffect — ProductDetailPanel will be the first
Prop types declared as local 'type Props = { ... }' above the function — existing pattern; no new props needed
edgeCases: Zero focusable elements: guard focusable list before calling [0].focus() or at(-1).focus() — close button always exists while open so list is never truly empty, but guard defensively
One focusable element (close button only, during loading/error states): Tab and Shift+Tab must wrap back to the same element (first === last); no-op movement is correct

document.activeElement is null or body at open time: capture it into prevFocusRef regardless; restore call must be guarded — if (prevFocusRef.current && prevFocusRef.current.isConnected) prevFocusRef.current.focus()

productId switches between two non-null values: useLayoutEffect depends on [productId] so it re-runs on each change — prev-focus is re-captured from the new document.activeElement on each product open
Escape key when focus is outside panel: document-level listener fires unconditionally — no contains() check should filter it
Escape listener must be removed in useEffect cleanup to prevent calling stale onClose on an already-closed panel
Backdrop and close-button both call onClose — both reach the same useLayoutEffect cleanup (productId → null) and restore focus correctly
Unmount while open: cleanup runs; check isConnected before restoring focus to avoid calling focus() on a detached node
useLayoutEffect keyed on productId: cleanup runs before the next effect run AND on unmount — both the restore path and the Escape cleanup must handle this

tasks.requirement: Requirement 1 and 5: useLayoutEffect keyed on productId; Requirement 7: noUnusedLocals means refs must be attached in JSX
tasks.description: Add closeButtonRef (useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null)) and prevFocusRef (useRef<Element | null>(null)) after the existing panelRef declaration. Attach closeButtonRef to the close button element in JSX (replacing or augmenting the existing button). These refs are prerequisites for the useLayoutEffect and Tab-trap logic.

tasks.requirement: Requirement 1: focus moves to close button on open using useLayoutEffect keyed on productId. Requirement 5: document.activeElement captured into ref before .focus(); restored when isOpen becomes false.
tasks.description: Add a useLayoutEffect that depends on [productId]. When productId is non-null: capture document.activeElement into prevFocusRef.current before calling any .focus(), then call closeButtonRef.current?.focus(). In the effect cleanup: call prevFocusRef.current?.focus() if prevFocusRef.current is non-null and isConnected, then reset prevFocusRef.current to null. Place this effect after the existing scroll-lock useEffect, before the if (!isOpen) return null guard.

tasks.requirement: Requirement 2: Tab on last focusable wraps to first. Requirement 3: Shift+Tab on first focusable wraps to last.
tasks.description: Add an onKeyDown handler function that: queries panelRef.current for all focusable elements matching 'button:not([disabled]), a[href], input:not([disabled]), select:not([disabled]), textarea:not([disabled]), [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])'; converts to array; identifies first and last; if Tab (no Shift) and activeElement is last, calls event.preventDefault() and firstFocusable.focus(); if Tab+Shift and activeElement is first, calls event.preventDefault() and lastFocusable.focus(). Attach this handler as onKeyDown on the panel div (the element with role='dialog').

tasks.requirement: Requirement 4: Escape calls onClose regardless of focus location. Listener attached via document.addEventListener inside a useEffect that depends on [isOpen], removed in cleanup.
tasks.description: Add a useEffect that depends on [isOpen, onClose]. When isOpen is true: create a keydown handler that checks event.key === 'Escape' and calls onClose(); attach it via document.addEventListener('keydown', handler); return a cleanup that calls document.removeEventListener('keydown', handler). When isOpen is false the effect runs but registers no listener (early return or conditional inside). Place this effect after the useLayoutEffect added in task-2.
